title: This $20 bill cost 7 cents to print. So why is it worth $20?

beats.text: This 20 dollar bill cost about 7 cents to print. So why is it worth 20? Let's go back to the start.
Before money, people swapped. Jake's fish for your shoes. But what if you hate fish?
So people used things everyone wanted. Shells, then coins of gold and silver, worth something on their own.
But metal is heavy. So China printed paper promises you could trade for coins.
Dollars worked the same way, backed by gold. Until 1971, when America cut that link.
So today the paper is worth 7 cents. It's worth 20 because the law says it pays any debt or tax, and because everyone trusts the next person will take it.
Money is just trust we all agree on. Would you still take it?
